title: Forward Engine Mount Bolt Bore — Detailed and Eddy Current Inspection
abstract: Detailed and eddy current inspection of the forward engine mount bolt bores at a scheduled engine removal, recording fretting depth and bore ovality in the parent material against the reworkable limits.

sections.purpose: This task gives the inspection of the four forward engine mount bolt bores with the engine removed, and the criteria that decide between a polish, a bushing installation and a fitting replacement. The limits are stated for the bore as machined in the parent material.
sections.job_setup_note: Do the inspection with the engine off and the pylon supported. The bores must be clean and dry; anti-seize compound in a bore gives an eddy current trace that looks like an indication. Confirm the calibration of the eddy current set against the reference block before the first bore and again after the last, and record both.
sections.procedure: Remove the engine to the standard procedure and support the pylon. Remove the pylon fairing panels to give access to the forward mount. Remove the titanium bolts LN569360-2A and the heat shield CAD50991-63 where fitted. Clean each bore with the approved solvent and dry it. CAUTION: REMOVE ALL ANTI-SEIZE COMPOUND FROM THE BORE BEFORE THE EDDY CURRENT SCAN. RESIDUAL COMPOUND GIVES A TRACE THAT CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM A SURFACE INDICATION. Do a detailed visual inspection of each bore under magnification and record the position and extent of any fretting. Measure the bore diameter at three angular positions and calculate the ovality. Calibrate the eddy current set against the reference block and record the calibration. Scan each bore with the probe for the parent bore diameter and record any indication with its position and amplitude. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER AN UNSUPPORTED PYLON. CONFIRM THAT THE PYLON SUPPORT IS IN POSITION AND LOADED BEFORE YOU GO UNDER IT. Compare each result against the limits in the illustration: inside the polish limit, polish and re-protect; between the polish limit and the reworkable limit, install a bushing; outside the reworkable limit, refer to Aeralis. Record the disposition for each bore.
sections.close_out: Apply the corrosion preventive compound to each bore that is left as inspected. Record the fretting depth, the ovality, the eddy current results and the disposition for all four bores, together with the airframe flight cycles. Report any bore outside the reworkable limit to Aeralis before any further work. Refit the heat shield and the mount bolts to the applicable installation task.

type_data.effectivity_note: TTN-88E1 aircraft with the CVX-7200 installation, bores in the parent material. The Auran installation has a different mount geometry and is not covered by this task.

safety_precautions: Do not work under an unsupported pylon.
Remove all anti-seize compound before the eddy current scan.
Confirm the eddy current calibration before and after the inspection.

tooling.description: Eddy current probe, 2 MHz, with bore adapter
Eddy current reference block, mount bore

title: Forward Engine Mount Bolt Bore — Detailed and Eddy Current Inspection

issue.reason: Bushed bore procedure added with its own reference block and probe, and the acceptance limits restated per bore standard.

abstract: Detailed and eddy current inspection of the forward engine mount bolt bores at a scheduled engine removal, in a parent bore branch and a bushed bore branch, recording fretting depth and ovality against the limits for the standard fitted.

sections.purpose: This task gives the inspection of the four forward engine mount bolt bores with the engine removed, and the criteria that decide between a polish, a bushing installation and a fitting replacement. The procedure, the reference block and the limits are stated per bore standard: a bushed bore is not a parent bore with a liner in it as far as this inspection is concerned.
sections.job_setup_note: Do the inspection with the engine off and the pylon supported. Establish the bore standard at each of the four positions from the aircraft record before you draw the equipment; the bushed bore takes its own probe and its own reference block, and the parent bore block will not calibrate against a bush interface. The bores must be clean and dry; anti-seize compound in a bore gives an eddy current trace that looks like an indication. Confirm the calibration of the eddy current set against the reference block for the standard being inspected, before the first bore and again after the last, and record both.
sections.procedure: Remove the engine to the standard procedure and support the pylon. Remove the pylon fairing panels to give access to the forward mount. Remove the titanium bolts LN569360-2A and the heat shield CAD50991-63 where fitted. Establish the bore standard at each position and select the branch for it. Clean each bore with the approved solvent and dry it. CAUTION: REMOVE ALL ANTI-SEIZE COMPOUND FROM THE BORE BEFORE THE EDDY CURRENT SCAN. RESIDUAL COMPOUND GIVES A TRACE THAT CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM A SURFACE INDICATION. Do a detailed visual inspection of each bore under magnification and record the position and extent of any fretting; on a bushed bore, examine the bush bore itself and the visible part of the bush interface, and record any relative movement witness mark. Measure the bore diameter at three angular positions and calculate the ovality against the limit for the standard fitted. Calibrate the eddy current set against the reference block for that standard and record the calibration. Scan each bore and record any indication with its position and amplitude. CAUTION: ON A BUSHED BORE THE BUSH INTERFACE RETURNS A CONTINUOUS INDICATION AROUND THE FULL CIRCUMFERENCE. THAT IS THE INTERFACE AND NOT A DEFECT. DO NOT READ IT AGAINST THE PARENT BORE LIMIT. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER AN UNSUPPORTED PYLON. CONFIRM THAT THE PYLON SUPPORT IS IN POSITION AND LOADED BEFORE YOU GO UNDER IT. Compare each result against the limits for the standard fitted: on a parent bore, inside the polish limit, polish and re-protect, between the polish limit and the reworkable limit, install a bushing, and outside the reworkable limit, refer to Aeralis. On a bushed bore, an indication that departs from the interface trace, or ovality of the bush bore beyond its own limit, means the bush is replaced; the parent bore is not reworked a second time. Record the disposition and the bore standard for each position.
sections.close_out: Apply the corrosion preventive compound to each bore that is left as inspected. Record the bore standard, the fretting depth, the ovality, the eddy current results with the reference block used, and the disposition for all four bores, together with the airframe flight cycles. A result recorded without the bore standard cannot be assessed and the position has to be inspected again. Report any bore outside the reworkable limit to Aeralis before any further work. Refit the heat shield and the mount bolts to the applicable installation task.

type_data.effectivity_note: TTN-88E1 aircraft with the CVX-7200 installation, in two branches by bore standard. The bushed bore branch applies at any position converted under MOD-144230, position by position; an aircraft may have both standards on one mount. The Auran installation has a different mount geometry and is not covered by this task.

safety_precautions: Do not work under an unsupported pylon.
Remove all anti-seize compound before the eddy current scan.
Confirm the eddy current calibration against the reference block for the bore standard, before and after the inspection.

tooling.description: Eddy current probe, 2 MHz, with bore adapter
Eddy current reference block, mount bore
